name: XPath Tester successor
demand: Available demand proxies are meaningful but do not establish paid demand: the original developer reported 20,000+ users, and an extension tracker records 20,000 installs and 107 ratings; these are not verified active users or buyers (https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg; https://extpose.com/ext/353731). As checked on 2026-10-23, Chrome Web Store listings show 6,000 users for an independent XPath Tester fork, 5,000 for XPath Selector, and 400,000 for SelectorsHub (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/nmjjcokoigamfoklbjmhpmjajmcjbjld?hl=en; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-selector/pjpaknobphgjgaembmafddoejmphpibk; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/selectorshub/ndgimibanhlabgdgjcpbbndiehljcpfh). These listings are not a deduplicated market size. Monthly search volume, active use, and willingness to pay for saved or shared suites: unverified.
prices: SelectorsHub’s vendor license page states Pro is $2.50/month; its current plans page lists a free tier, up to 10 saved values free, up to 50 on Premium, and a Team plan with central billing and member management, but does not show a numerical current checkout price or team price (https://selectorshub.com/selectorshub-license/; https://www.selectorshub.com/selectorshub-pro/plans/). XPath Tester and XPath Selector listings disclose no paid tier or price; XPath Helper Pro is also listed without a price (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/nmjjcokoigamfoklbjmhpmjajmcjbjld?hl=en; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-selector/pjpaknobphgjgaembmafddoejmphpibk; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-helper-pro/ncdgoaeicnckepaccgbdjbejiimnfhid?hl=en-US). Selector Forge offers a free tier of 200 selectors per month and unlimited use on a paid Intuned plan; exact plan price is unverified here (https://selectorforge.ai/; https://intunedhq.com/blog/selector-forge).

revenue_proof.claim: The original developer said users included paid subscribers after the extension was removed. This is a dated first-party statement, not independently verified transaction evidence; payer count and revenue are unverified.
SelectorsHub publicly offers a paid Pro tier and states $2.50/month on its license page. This verifies a posted price, not sales or revenue; the current checkout price is unverified.
revenue_proof.claim_event_date: 2026-10-23 page check; effective date of stated price unverified

copy_speed: At least two relevant releases are documented after April 2026: a new XPath Tester listing was created 2026-06-17 and includes free local History and Saved features; its Chrome Web Store listing now shows 68 users (https://chrome-stats.com/d/lleffifhlcaijinkocppghpgbnioechc; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/lleffifhlcaijinkocppghpgbnioechc). Selector Forge launched 2026-06-19 with AI-generated CSS/XPath selectors, Chrome and Firefox support, and an open-source codebase (https://intunedhq.com/blog/selector-forge; https://github.com/Intuned/selector-forge). XPath Tool’s July 2026 update added a side panel and improved iframe and Shadow DOM handling; its listing history shows it was not a new launch (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tool/cpcnmjjlfdpicppncnambopmefpienej).
platform_risk: High platform concentration. The original listing was removed in May 2026 and its former Chrome Web Store URL now resolves to an empty-title page; the original developer reported that appeals and a resubmission did not restore it, while the specific removal cause remains unverified (https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/cneomjecgakdfoeehmmmoiklncdiodmh). A Chrome Extensions representative said on 2026-07-07 that third-party monetization is allowed, but policies still apply and paywall libraries must be disclosed in the listing; Chrome policy also requires clear payment disclosures and restricts duplicate experiences from the same or related developers (https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg; https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/policies/). This does not prove that paid extensions generally are at risk, but the original product is a direct warning about relying on one store.
defensible_asset: No UK-specific data asset or rules engine is apparent for a global browser developer tool. A potentially defensible asset would be accumulated team-shared test suites, change history, and integrations, but that value is unproven and existing products already cover pieces of it: SelectorsHub offers saved values and team account management, while the June 2026 XPath Tester offers local saved queries (https://www.selectorshub.com/selectorshub-pro/plans/; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/lleffifhlcaijinkocppghpgbnioechc). CSS Selector & XPath Finder also offers team syncing and shareable browser artifacts, although that is broader than XPath test suites (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/css-selector-xpath-finder/bmgbagkoginmbbgjapcacehjdojdnnhf).
build_effort: Estimate, not a sourced benchmark: roughly 30–60 agent-assisted hours for a local-first extension with live XPath testing, highlighting, and local saved suites; add roughly 80–140 hours for accounts, secure cloud sharing, team roles, billing, and operational handling. Routine code drafting, documentation, and support triage could be agent-assisted, but browser compatibility checks, release review, billing exceptions, and policy responses still need owner oversight. The local workflow exists in current extensions, while the proposed team and paid features add most of the complexity (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/nmjjcokoigamfoklbjmhpmjajmcjbjld?hl=en; https://www.selectorshub.com/selectorshub-pro/plans/).
channel: Use Chrome Web Store search placement, technical SEO/tutorials, an ungated useful free tier, and opt-in beta signups; promote publicly only in developer communities that permit it. Do not rely on cold email, SMS, WhatsApp, or social DMs to individuals or sole traders: ICO guidance treats sole traders as individual subscribers and includes social DMs in electronic mail, for which consent or a valid soft opt-in is generally required. The ICO says its B2B guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act, so recheck it before any campaign (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/direct-marketing-guidance/plan-direct-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Estimate: 4–7 hours/week once stable, so the <=5-hour constraint is not assured; 10–20 hours/week during launch and early support. A local-only free tool could be lower-maintenance, but the paid shared-team tier adds account, billing, privacy, and support work.
desk_test: Within one day and at $0: review-code public feedback for the removed XPath Tester and current SelectorsHub, XPath Tester, and XPath Selector listings. Tag only explicit requests for reusable suites, team sharing, or paid workflows; do not count install totals, ratings, or complaints about a paywall as evidence of revenue. Use a pre-set gate such as five independent, recent requests for shared suites before building; the original listing’s available review snapshot and current store listings provide starting material (https://extpose.com/ext/353731; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/selectorshub/ndgimibanhlabgdgjcpbbndiehljcpfh; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/lleffifhlcaijinkocppghpgbnioechc; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-selector/pjpaknobphgjgaembmafddoejmphpibk). This is a pain-point screen, not proof of willingness to pay.
red_flags: The initial survive verdict should be revisited: the proposed individual saved-suite feature is already available free or in a low-cost tier, and team management or shareable artifacts exist in adjacent tools. The original product’s reported user base did not establish its revenue, and the only claim of paying users found is first-party. A narrower team regression-suite workflow might still merit a test, but that differentiation and paid demand are unverified (https://www.selectorshub.com/selectorshub-pro/plans/; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/xpath-tester/lleffifhlcaijinkocppghpgbnioechc; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/css-selector-xpath-finder/bmgbagkoginmbbgjapcacehjdojdnnhf; https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg).
